children: Welcome back. Russia has turned up the heat on Kyiv's allies in Europe with a string of so-called gray zone activities aimed at sowing fear.

European authorities have linked Russia to a spate of drone incursions, acts of sabotage, cyberattacks and other hostile actions across the continent over recent months. New U.S. intelligence reports assess that Russia could try to test NATO's resolve with a limited assault on a member country in the next few years, through steps potentially ranging from a cyberattack to a small-scale land incursion. Read more from WSJ .

Boston Scientific heart monitoring devices are impeded after a cyberattack, the company said. Cardiac rhythm management devices implanted after the Aug. 25 hack can't be activated to send data to remote patient management systems, the company said. Episodes will continue to be recorded and will be transmitted when Boston Scientific's internal tech systems are restored and the affected devices can be paired with patient apps and home-monitoring equipment, according to the company.

In addition to order processing and shipping, manufacturing has also been disrupted, the company said. Factory shifts have been canceled at facilities in Ireland and workers' daily schedules have been upended, the Irish Examiner reported.

Hospitals and other customers can place orders but they won't be fulfilled until on-premises tech is restored. "We are expeditiously working toward partial restoration for the shipping of some products this week," the company said in a notice on its website.

Pharmaceuticals distributor McKesson said data related to customers of its oncology and multispecialty business unit, as well as its medical-surgical unit, was stolen in a cyber incident detected Aug. 25 that affected certain third-party applications. An investigation is ongoing.

Hasbro is notifying employees that their personal and financial data was compromised in a March cyberattack. The incident has so far cost the toy maker $11 million, and lost revenue of around $25 million, Hasbro said in its most recent earnings report. (CyberNews)

Cyber Command suicides: Officials with U.S. Cyber Command are due to meet Sept. 3 with House Armed Services Committee staff to discuss a rise in deaths by suicide in the unit. As many as five people who work in or work closely with Cyber Command died by suicide between June and July, Bloomberg reported. Burnout and psychological strain have been ongoing concerns for the command and lawmakers.

The CyberIndex rose 6.5% last week, buoyed by Okta's 25% gain and CrowdStrike's 13%. Rubrik registered the biggest losses in the period, dropping 5% over the week. It was the only cyber stock to lose more than 1%.
